item.content:encoded:
Mientras marchamos por la última semana de la temporada regular, no parece haber mucho suspenso respecto a quiénes serán nombrados JMV. Al menos, eso es lo que podemos descifrar de nuestra más reciente -- y última -- encuesta del JMV de MLB.com para el 2026.
El cubano Yordan Álvarez sigue estando bien al frente en la Liga Americana a pesar de una producción relativamente mediocre recientemente. En la Liga Nacional, Pete Crow-Armstrong está cerrando una de las mejores campañas completas en tiempos recientes.
Treinta y ocho expertos de MLB.com emitieron sus votos sobre quiénes creen que se llevarán los honores de JMV tras esta temporada, con 32 jugadores recibiendo al menos un voto. Como recordatorio, los votos se basaron no solo en el desempeño hasta ahora, sino también en cómo se espera que evolucionen las cosas durante el resto de la campaña.
Los votantes clasificaron a sus cinco principales candidatos de cada liga con un sistema de 5-4-3-2-1: cinco puntos por un voto al primer lugar, cuatro por el segundo, y así sucesivamente. Estos son los resultados.
Todas las estadísticas son hasta la jornada del domingo, a menos que se indique lo contrario.
LIGA AMERICANA
Álvarez ha tenido un desempeño tan bueno este año que lo que califica como un bache para él sería un gran trecho para la mayoría de los demás bateadores. En sus últimos 41 encuentros, batea .264 con OPS de .840. Reiteramos, nada mal para la mayoría, pero muy por debajo del nivel del líder de la Americana en promedio (.313) y OPS (1.027). Álvarez lleva tres cuadrangulares y cinco impulsadas a lo largo de 16 partidos este mes, dejándolo a un jonrón del dominicano Junior Caminero de los Rays por el liderato en el Joven Circuito y a seis empujadas de Pete Alonso por la cima en dicho departamento. Aunque sus posibilidades de la Triple Corona se están desvaneciendo un poco, Álvarez todavía ha armado un 2026 asombroso en el plato. Su wRC+ de 179 es al menos 27 puntos mejor que el de cualquier otro bateador calificado.
Sabemos que el quisqueyano es uno de los grandes cañoneros del juego. Está cerrando su segunda temporada consecutiva de 40 vuelacercas y está dando swings más fuerte que nadie. Pero lo que ha sido más impresionante de su temporada es su mejorado criterio en la zona de strike. Aumentó su tasa de boletos desde un 6.3% por debajo del promedio a un 11.5%, lo que se ubica en el 80mo percentil de MLB. También ha mantenido una tasa de ponches muy sólida (18.5%). Ya no persigue tantos pitcheos fuera de la zona, ha reducido su tasa de swings en blanco y está haciendo más contacto en general. Esa mezcla de paciencia, trueno y control del bate es una combinación especial, sobre todo en un jugador de 23 años. Luciendo un porcentaje de embasarse de .363 (52 puntos mejor que la campaña pasada), el OPS de .892 de Caminero se ubica tercero en la Americana.
Witt ha tenido mejores campañas a la ofensiva, aunque 18 bambinazos, 43 estafadas y wRC+ de 119 en 137 partidos no está nada mal. Pero cuando se consideran todas sus capacidades, Witt sigue siendo extremadamente valioso. Su valor de carreras defensivas de +16 está empatado en el tercer lugar de las Grandes Ligas, y sus 22 outs por encima del promedio encabezan la Liga Americana. También cuenta con un valor de carreras en el corrido de bases de +8, a uno de Corbin Carroll de los Diamondbacks por el liderato de MLB. Por eso, aunque no ha sido tan indiscutible en la caja de bateo como lo fue en el 2024 (wRC+ de 169), la grandeza integral de Witt lo tiene en la cima de la tabla de posiciones de WAR de FanGraphs en el Joven Circuito (6.6) y posiblemente perfilándolo entre los primeros cinco en la votación para JMV por tercera vez en tres años.
Ha habido bastante conversación de JMV entorno a Schlittler en las últimas semanas. ¿Y por qué no? Está marcando el paso en la Americana en efectividad (1.94), WHIP (0.91) y WAR de pitcheo de FanGraphs (6.1). Se ubica segundo en el Joven Circuito en promedio de bateo en contra (.182) y en tasa de ponches menos boletos (25.0%). Ha permitido una carrera o ninguna en 21 aperturas. Ese es un récord de la franquicia de los Yankees y algo que apenas otros dos lanzadores de 25 años o menos han logrado en la Era de la Pelota Viva (desde 1920): Blake Snell (2018) y Dean Chance (1964). Seguramente será reconocido con el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana a estas alturas, pero Schlittler recibirá su merecida cuota de consideración para el JMV.
Schlittler no ha sido el único miembro de los Bombarderos que ha sido indispensable este año. Mientras Nueva York ha estado sin Aaron Judge durante una gran parte de la campaña y ha echado de menos a otros bates estelares debido a lesiones, Rice ha sido demostrado consistencia. Se ubica tercero en el Joven Circuito en jonrones (39) y anotadas (100). Es cuarto en la liga en impulsadas (95) y OPS (.888), y está empatado en el cuarto lugar en valor de carreras al bate (+34). Con dos vuelacercas durante la última semana, Rice se convertiría en apenas el segundo miembro del equipo del Bronx diferente a Judge en la última década en conectar al menos 41 jonrones en una temporada, acompañando al dominicano Juan Soto (2024).
Otros que recibieron votos: El venezolano Willson Contreras, Medias Rojas; Pete Alonso, Orioles; Kevin McGonigle, Tigres; el cubano Miguel Vargas, Medias Blancas; el cubano Randy Arozarena, Marineros; Munetaka Murakami, Medias Blancas; Dylan Cease, Azulejos.
LIGA NACIONAL
El mes pasado, PCA dio el salto por encima de Ohtani hacia el puesto Nro. 1 de nuestra encuesta. Este mes, se ha apartado por completo del resto del grupo. Crow-Armstrong, quien recibió cada voto de primer lugar emitido por nuestro panel, está empatado con Kyle Schwarber en el liderato de bambinazos de MLB (45). Nadie tiene más anotadas (118), extrabases (83) o total de bases anotadas (351) esta campaña. Con 38 estafadas, el dinámico jardinero central del equipo del Norte de Chicago podría convertirse en el séptimo miembro del club 40-40 más adelante esta semana. Y no pase por alto el hecho de que es posiblemente el mejor jugador a la defensa en cualquier posición en estos momentos. Ya no es una cuestión de si Crow-Armstrong es el JMV de la Nacional. El premio es prácticamente suyo ahora mismo. Pero ¿lo ganará de manera unánime?
Ohtani se mantiene como el claro escolta en el Viejo Circuito a pesar de haber jugado en apenas tres partidos este mes debido a sus persistentes lesiones en la rodilla izquierda y el bíceps derecho. La buena noticia es que el dirigente de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, dijo que "hay una buena posibilidad" de que Ohtani sea activado de la lista de lesionados de 15 días el miércoles tras cumplir la estadía mínima. No lanzará por el resto de la temporada, dejándolo con efectividad de 1.79 y 95 ponches en 85.2 entradas. Pero Ohtani tendrá unos cuantos partidos para sumar a sus totales ofensivos (30 jonrones, wRC+ de 142).
Mencionamos antes cómo Schlittler luce como el gran favorito para el Premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana. Misiorowski tendría su premio más asegurado en la Nacional. A lo largo de 169.1 episodios, Miz encabeza la Gran Carpa en casi cada categoría, incluyendo efectividad (1.86), WHIP (0.80), tasa de ponches menos boletos (31.7%) y fWAR (6.5), por nombrar solo algunas. Sus oponentes tienen un diminuto OPS de .474 contra Misiorowski, la segunda menor cifra para cualquier abridor calificado en la Era Divisional (desde 1969). Los oponentes del quisqueyano Pedro Martínez, en una de las mejores campañas para un lanzador, registraron OPS de .473 en el 2000.
El dominicano, quien no recibió un solo voto en nuestra anterior encuesta de JMV, ha estado encendido con Cincinnati durante el último mes. En sus últimos 27 encuentros, batea .404 con ocho vuelacercas, seis bases robadas y OPS de 1.205. Dio múltiples hits en 14 de esos partidos, y su fWAR de 2.5 durante este transcurso es el mejor de las Mayores. Esta prolongada racha encendida le ha dado a De la Cruz un wRC+ de 139 -- el mejor de su carrera -- y lo deja a dos jonrones más dos estafadas de convertirse en el cuarto jugador de los Rojos en el club 30-30 y el primero desde Brandon Phillips en el 2007.
Schwarber ha caído en un pequeño bache, bateando de 34-4 con un cuadrangular en sus últimos 10 encuentros. También está a ocho ponches de establecer un récord de ponches en una misma campaña. De todas maneras, hay que admirar la consistencia de Schwarber. Terminará con más de 40 vuelacercas y 150 juegos disputados en cuatro de las últimas cinco temporadas. Ha superado los 100 boletos negociados por cuarto año consecutivo, y un tercer título de bambinazos del Viejo Circuito está a su alcance.
Otros que recibieron votos: El dominicano Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres; Brice Turang, Cerveceros; Matt Olson, Bravos; James Wood, Nacionales; Jordan Walker, Cardenales; Alex Bregman, Cachorros; Bryce Harper, Filis; Jake Bauers, Cerveceros; el dominicano Otto López, Marlins; el venezolano Gabriel Moreno, Diamondbacks; el dominicano Rafael Devers, Gigantes; Alec Burleson, Cardenales; CJ Abrams, Nacionales; Corbin Carroll, Diamondbacks; el dominicano Cristopher Sánchez, Filis.

item.content:encoded:
As we make our way through the final week of the regular season, there doesn't seem to be much suspense as to who will be named MVP. At least, that's what we can glean from our latest -- and final -- MLB.com 2026 MVP poll.
Yordan Alvarez is still well out in front in the American League despite relatively mediocre production of late. In the National League, Pete Crow-Armstrong is wrapping up one of the best all-around seasons in recent memory.
Thirty-eight MLB.com experts cast votes for who they think will earn MVP honors after this season, with 32 players receiving at least one vote. As a reminder, votes were based not only on results so far, but also on how things are expected to play out the rest of the season.
Voters ranked their top five picks in each league on a 5-4-3-2-1 scale -- five points for a first-place vote, four points for a second-place vote and so on. Here are the results.
All stats are through Sunday unless otherwise noted.
AMERICAN LEAGUE
Alvarez has been so good this year that what qualifies as a slump for him would be a good stretch for most other hitters. Over his past 41 games, he is hitting .264 with an .840 OPS. Again, not bad for most, but well below the standard of the AL leader in average (.313) and OPS (1.027). Alvarez has three homers and five RBIs through 16 games this month, leaving him tied with the O's Pete Alonso and one home run behind the Rays' Junior Caminero for the AL lead and nine RBIs behind Alonso for the top spot in that statistic. Even though his Triple Crown chances have faded, Alvarez has still put together an awesome 2026 at the plate. His 179 wRC+ is at least 27 points better than any other qualified hitter.
We know Caminero is one of the game's great sluggers. He is finishing up his second straight 40-homer season and swings harder than anyone. But what's been most impressive about his season is his improved strike-zone judgment. He has upped his walk rate from a below-average 6.3% to 11.5%, which ranks in the 80th percentile of MLB. He's also maintained a very solid strikeout rate (18.5%). He's not chasing as much, has shaved his whiff rate and is making more contact overall. That blend of patience, power and bat control is a special combination, especially in a 23-year-old player. Carrying a .363 on-base percentage (52 points better than last season), Caminero's .892 OPS ranks third in the AL.
Witt has had better offensive seasons, although 18 homers, 43 steals and a 119 wRC+ in 137 games is not too shabby. But when you consider his entire skill set, Witt remains extremely valuable. His +16 fielding run value is tied for third in the Majors, and his 22 outs above average tops the AL. He also has a +8 baserunning run value, one behind the D-backs' Corbin Carroll for the MLB lead. So while he hasn't been as undeniable in the batter's box as he was in 2024 (169 wRC+), Witt's all-around greatness has him atop the AL FanGraphs WAR leaderboard (6.6) and in line for a possible top-five finish in the MVP voting for the third time in three years.
There has been quite a bit of MVP chatter surrounding Schlittler in recent weeks. And why not? He is pacing the AL in ERA (1.94), WHIP (0.91) and FanGraphs pitching WAR (6.1). He ranks second in the junior circuit in opponents' batting average (.182) and strikeout-minus-walk rate (25.0%). He has allowed one or zero runs in 21 starts. That's a Yankees franchise record and something only two other pitchers age-25 or younger have accomplished in the Live Ball Era (since 1920): Blake Snell (2018) and Dean Chance (1964). He seems like a lock for the AL Cy Young Award at this point, but Schlittler will receive his fair share of MVP love.
Schlittler hasn't been the only indispensable Yankee this year. While New York has been without Aaron Judge for a large portion of the season and has missed other star bats as well due to injuries, Rice has been a constant. He ranks third in the AL in homers (39) and runs scored (100). He's fourth in the league in RBIs (95) and OPS (.888), and tied for fourth in batting run value (+34). With two homers during the final week, Rice would become just the second non-Judge Yankee over the past decade to hit at least 41 homers in a season, joining Juan Soto (2024).
Others receiving votes: Willson Contreras, Red Sox; Pete Alonso, Orioles; Kevin McGonigle, Tigers; Miguel Vargas, White Sox; Randy Arozarena, Mariners; Munetaka Murakami, White Sox; Dylan Cease, Blue Jays
NATIONAL LEAGUE
Last month, PCA jumped over Ohtani and into the No. 1 spot in our poll. This month, he has run away from the rest of the field. The recipient of every first-place vote cast by our panel, Crow-Armstrong is tied with Kyle Schwarber for the MLB lead in home runs (45). No one has more runs (118), extra-base hits (83) or total bases (351) this season. With 38 steals, the Cubs' dynamic center fielder could become the seventh member of the 40-40 club later this week. Oh, and let's not overlook the fact that he is arguably the best defensive player at any position right now. It's no longer a question of whether Crow-Armstrong is the NL MVP. The award is as good as his right now. But will he win it in unanimous fashion?
Ohtani remains the clear runner-up in the NL despite playing in just three games this month due to his nagging left knee and right biceps injuries. The good news is Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said "there's a good chance" Ohtani will be activated from the 15-day injured list Wednesday after a minimum stint. He won't pitch for the rest of the season, leaving him with a 1.79 ERA and 95 K's over 85 2/3 innings. But Ohtani will have a few games to add to his offensive totals (30 homers, 142 wRC+).
We mentioned earlier how Schlittler looks like the heavy favorite for the AL Cy Young Award. Misiorowski is an even bigger shoo-in in the senior circuit. Through 169 1/3 innings, Miz leads the Majors in just about every category, including ERA (1.86), WHIP (0.80), strikeout-minus-walk rate (31.7%) and fWAR (6.5), to name just a few. Opposing batters have a scant .474 OPS against Misiorowski, which is the second-lowest by any qualified starter in the Divisional Era (since 1969). Pedro Martinez, in one of the greatest seasons by a pitcher, recorded a .473 opponents' OPS in 2000.
De La Cruz, who didn't receive a single vote in our previous MVP poll, has been red-hot for Cincinnati over the past month. In his last 27 games, he is batting .404 with eight homers, six steals and a 1.205 OPS. He collected multiple hits in 14 of those games, and his 2.5 fWAR during this period is the best in the big leagues. This prolonged hot streak has given De La Cruz a career-best 139 wRC+ and has left him two homers and two steals away from becoming the fourth Red in the 30-30 club and the first since Brandon Phillips in 2007.
Schwarber has fallen into a bit of a rut, going 4-for-34 with one home run over his past 10 games. He's also eight strikeouts away from setting a new record for K's in a single season. Even so, you have to admire Schwarber's consistency. He will end up with more than 40 homers and 150 games played in four of the past five seasons. He has surpassed 100 walks for a fourth consecutive season, and a third NL home run title is right there for the taking, too.
Others receiving votes: Fernando Tatis Jr., Padres; Brice Turang, Brewers; Matt Olson, Braves; James Wood, Nationals; Jordan Walker, Cardinals; Alex Bregman, Cubs; Bryce Harper, Phillies; Jake Bauers, Brewers; Otto Lopez, Marlins; Gabriel Moreno, Diamondbacks; Rafael Devers, Giants; Alec Burleson, Cardinals; CJ Abrams, Nationals; Corbin Carroll, Diamondbacks; Cristopher Sánchez, Phillies

Sep 21, 2026, 10:38 PM ET
Across 572 plate appearances in 2026, Arizona Diamondbacks third baseman Nolan Arenado is hitting .247/.322/.455 with 27 home runs, 78 RBI, 73 runs scored, and four stolen bases. After hitting just 28 home runs across over 1,000 plate appearances in his final two seasons with the St. Louis Cardinals in 2024 and 2025, it's been a resurgent campaign for the 35-year-old. Arenado has also been red-hot of late, hitting .317 with six home runs and 13 RBI across 68 plate appearances in September. Arenado also has a favorable schedule in the final week of the regular season, as the Diamondbacks will open a three-game set at Coors Field against the Colorado Rockies on Tuesday. In any league where he is available on the waiver wire, Arenado profiles as a priority target for fantasy managers.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
More Recent News
Sep 21, 2026, 10:59 PM ET
Across 348 plate appearances since making his MLB debut in early June, Colorado Rockies outfielder/shortstop Cole Carrigg is hitting .271/.335/.461 with 10 home runs, 48 RBI, 46 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases. The 24-year-old has been a balanced producer for fantasy managers for most of the second half of the season. However, he's been particularly hot in recent weeks. Across 77 plate appearances in September, Carrigg is hitting .307 with four home runs, 12 RBI, eight runs scored, and three stolen bases. Carrigg also has a favorable schedule to end the year, with three games at home against the Arizona Diamondbacks followed by three games in Chicago against the White Sox. In leagues where he remains available on the waiver wire, Carrigg profiles as an outfield streamer for fantasy managers to target.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Sep 21, 2026, 10:47 PM ET
Across 431 plate appearances in 2026, Texas Rangers third baseman Josh Jung is hitting .295/.360/.450 with 11 home runs, 39 RBI, 52 runs scored, and one stolen base. After suffering a calf injury in late July, Jung missed almost two months' worth of action. However, the 28-year-old has hit well since returning to the Rangers lineup on September 12. Across his last 35 plate appearances, Jung is hitting .303 with two home runs, four RBI, and six runs scored. Jung has posted a career-best 48.7% hard-hit rate in 2026 while also dropping his strikeout rate to a career-low 18.1%. In fantasy leagues where he's not already rostered, Jung could be worth targeting on the waiver wire for the final week of the 2026 season.--Will Brady
Source: RotoBaller
Robert Suarez Expected to Return This Week


Will Brady




Sep 21, 2026, 10:29 PM ET
Atlanta Braves general manager Alex Anthopoulos said during a radio appearance on 680 The Fan that right-hander Robert Suarez (elbow) is "highly likely" to be activated from the 60-day injured list on either Wednesday or Thursday. Suarez has been sidelined since mid-June by inflammation in his right elbow, but it appears he will be back in the Atlanta bullpen for the team's postseason push. Across 32 innings (31 games) before suffering the injury, Suarez recorded a 0.56 ERA, 0.84 WHIP, 26 strikeouts, and four saves. While the 35-year-old's strikeout rate dropped to 21.5%, he allowed just one home run (0.28 HR/9). Upon his return, Suarez should be a key part of the bridge to Braves closer Raisel Iglesias.--Will Brady
Source: 680 The Fan
Sep 21, 2026, 10:20 PM ET
San Francisco Giants outfielder Jung Hoo Lee (groin) has been placed on the 10-day injured list with a groin contusion, per Justice delos Santos of The Mercury News. With less than 10 days remaining in the regular season, Lee's 2026 campaign is over. Across 579 plate appearances for the year, Lee hit .276/.320/.404 with 10 home runs, 57 RBI, 65 runs scored, and 12 stolen bases. The 28-year-old has a firm ceiling on his power, as he owns just a 3.1% barrel rate and a 33% hard-hit rate for his career. However, Lee struck out in fewer than 10% of his plate appearances this season and should continue to provide fantasy managers with a solid batting average and run production in 2027. With Lee sidelined, Giants outfielder Bo Davidson could take over as the team's everyday right fielder.--Will Brady
Source: The Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Willy Adames Returns to Baseball Activities


Will Brady




Sep 21, 2026, 10:12 PM ET
San Francisco Giants shortstop Willy Adames (elbow) fielded ground balls and took batting practice on Monday, per Justice delos Santos of The Mercury News. Adames has been sidelined since late August by an elbow injury and is unlikely to play again in 2026. However, the 31-year-old appears to be making progress and should have a relatively normal offseason heading into 2027. Across 505 plate appearances in 2026, Adames hit .230/.289/.424 with 21 home runs, 51 RBI, 62 runs scored, and six stolen bases. The veteran shortstop's barrel (8.9%) and hard-hit (38.8%) rates were both his worst since the 2019 season. Adames also graded out as one of the worst defensive shortstops in MLB, which is usually one of the strengths of his game. If the elbow injury was impacting his performance before he was finally placed on the injured list, Adames could be a worthy buy-low target for fantasy managers in 2027.--Will Brady
Source: The Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Bryce Eldridge Finishes Year on Concussion Injured List


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 7:24 PM ET
The San Francisco Giants placed rookie first baseman Bryce Eldridge (concussion) on the seven-day concussion injured list on Monday, ending his first full season with just a week left to play, according to Justice delos Santos of The San Jose Mercury News. The 21-year-old left-handed slugger had a cup of coffee with San Fran in 2025, playing in only 10 games, but he finishes 2026 with 107 games played at the major-league level. In those 107 games (448 plate appearances), Eldridge showed plenty of power potential at Oracle Park, slashing .269/.364/.461 with an .825 OPS, 17 homers, 57 RBI, 50 runs scored, and one stolen base. It was a disappointing end to the year, though, as he suffered a concussion when he hit his head at the team's hotel. The former first-rounder also hit .333 (38-for-114) with five homers and 22 RBI in 30 games at Triple-A Sacramento in 2026. One of the Giants' top prospects, outfielder Bo Davidson, and infielder Marcelo Mayer will get a chance to impress over the final week of the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The San Jose Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Troy Melton Lands on Injured List With Arm Fatigue


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 7:08 PM ET
The Detroit Tigers announced on Monday that they placed right-hander Troy Melton (forearm) on the 15-day injured list with right-arm fatigue and recalled right-handed pitching prospect River Ryan from Triple-A Toledo in a corresponding move. Melton felt something in his right forearm during his final outing of the season on Sunday in an 8-1 loss to the division-rival Chicago White Sox, allowing four earned runs on four hits while walking three and striking out four in 3 2/3 innings to pick up his fifth loss of the year. The 25-year-old former fourth-round pick in 2022 from San Diego State University had a strong second season in the majors altogether, going 8-5 with a 2.76 ERA (4.09 FIP) and 1.13 WHIP with 94 strikeouts and 37 walks in 114 1/3 innings across his 20 starts. Melton produced an identical 2.76 ERA in his MLB debut in 2025, too, in 16 appearances (four starts) covering 45 2/3 frames. A deep pitch mix with strong command makes Melton an intriguing and ascending young arm for fantasy managers going into the 2027 season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Tigers PR
Giants Calling Up Outfield Prospect Bo Davidson


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 6:52 PM ET
The San Francisco Giants are calling up outfield prospect Bo Davidson, the team's No. 8 prospect per MLB Pipeline, to the big leagues on Monday, a source told Justice delos Santos of The San Jose Mercury News. Davidson will get the call to the big leagues to begin the final week of the 2026 regular season after hitting .309/.389/.534 with 10 home runs and six steals for Triple-A Sacramento this year in 52 games across 234 plate appearances. He also hit .277/.340/.521 with an .861 OPS, 19 homers, 53 RBI, 14 steals, and 49 runs scored in 73 games and 315 plate appearances at Double-A Richmond. Obviously, it is too late in the season for Davidson to do any real damage in fantasy baseball leagues, but the Gigantes will get a look at one of their best position-player prospects in the final week, with both outfielder Jung Hoo Lee (groin) and Bryce Eldridge (head) currently dealing with injuries. The 24-year-old left-handed hitter has primarily played center field in the minors, but he could be used in a corner-outfield spot as well. Davidson has intriguing raw power from the left side and could push for an early MLB return in 2027 if he starts out hot in the minors.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The San Jose Mercury News - Justice delos Santos
Dylan Cease Will Not Need Shoulder Surgery


Keith Hernandez




Sep 21, 2026, 5:58 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Dylan Cease (shoulder) said he will not need surgery on his right shoulder following his MRI results, according to Hazel Mae of Sportsnet. Cease is now in "limbo" on what his next steps are, depending on where the team is in the American League playoff picture. The talented right-hander described his shoulder feeling as a "bit heavy and achy and not normal. But at the same time, it didn't feel like it was torn... not something I need surgery for or anything like that. It was just inflammation, just the kind of that middle ground." Toronto heads into Monday's series opener on the road against the division-rival Baltimore Orioles three games back of the final wild-card spot in the AL with six games left to play. If the Jays are still alive by the weekend, Cease could make his final start of the 2026 season at home against the Cincinnati Reds. The 30-year-old has had a banner year in Toronto in his first year with the club, going 11-6 with a 2.40 ERA, league-leading 2.55 FIP, a 1.10 WHIP, a career-high 239 strikeouts, and 78 walks in 169 innings and 29 starts.--Keith Hernandez

item.content:encoded:
Every Monday, this column will break down the most popular waiver wire and free agent acquisitions from the weekend. I dig into the top adds on the ever-popular Fantrax and in the NFBC Online Championship (OC), a national mid-stakes contest with 240 total leagues of 12 and a six-figure grand prize. Reviewing player adds between the two should provide us with a well-rounded perspective and barometer of the fantasy baseball marketplace.
Week 26 Overview
Hitters
The San Diego Padres took advantage of their four-game series with the Rockies at Coors Field and a home set with the Marlins, scoring 51 runs, 12 more than any other team. Fernando Tatis Jr. (along with Brandon Lowe and Pete Crow-Armstrong) led the way with a week-high four dingers. Last week’s streamers turned out to be dynamite: Jake Cronenworth (.464-8-2-8-2), Dustin Harris (.379-5-0-7-2) and Samad Taylor (.556-6-1-7-1) really stepped up, particularly Taylor for my competitive Main Event squad that gained two category points in batting average last week. Rake Cronenworth was true to his nickname from several years ago. He led all Major League hitters with 13 hits. The Brewers swiped a league-high 12 bags last week: four each for Jackson Chourio and rookie Cooper Pratt. Tampa’s Chandler Simpson led all runners with five swipes, finally catching Washington’s Nasim Nuñez for the MLB lead with 46. Expect Simpson to finish with 50+ and win the stolen base crown.
Pitchers
Of the 29 two-start pitchers excluding Pirates opener Lake Bachar, three earned two wins: Tarik Skubal, Sean Burke and David Peterson. Houston’s Hunter Brown had an outstanding two-step (10 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 5 K – 20 K) and those 20 punchouts led all pitchers for the week. Gavin Williams punched out 16 in 12 innings and is back atop the AL lead in strikeouts with 244. Dylan Cease (239) may not make his final start of the season and Cam Schlittler (234) is unlikely to catch Williams as both have one start remaining. It’s very possible that Williams catches and passes Jacob Misiorowski (247) for the Major League lead. The Miz pitched three innings in his weekend start and might be limited for his final one.
Tampa’s Bryan Baker was the first reliever to reach 40 saves this season. It’s possible that Cade Smith (39), Riley O’Brien (38) and Mason Miller (37) join Baker. The last time there were three closers with 40 or more saves was in 2019: Edwin Díaz (57), Wade Davis (43), and Craig Kimbrel (42). Shout out to folks who drafted O’Brien late, and/or picked up Baker, Louis Varland or Jacob Latz off waivers and didn’t have to worry about the saves category all season.
Week 27 Most Added Players: NFBC Main Event, NFBC OC, and Fantrax
It’s the last hurrah for managers with FAB dollars left, hoping to get the best bang for the buck and for variance to lean their way and tip them into league titles. As is usually the case in the final week, we hope to optimize our pitching rotations and hitters in hitter-friendly ballparks against bad pitching. It was odd seeing Shohei Ohtani available in several leagues, and perhaps fortuitous as he should be activated this week and start a few games. Ohtani was acquired in 26 OCs for an AWB of $17. In Main Events, there were 12 shares available and they went for a reasonable $12 a pop. I scooped up a rare Ohtani share in an OC for $2, winning a tiebreaker over the team in 1st place in that league. Andy Pages will be activated on Tuesday, which should push Tommy Edman back to second base. Pages had been out since August 21, but was producing at an exciting clip before the injury — .272 – 72 R – 21 HR – 80 RBI – 12 SB in 550 PA. Managers who acquired him are hoping that he dusts the cobwebs back off and gets right into the swing of things, with all the marbles on the line.

Pitchers were the most popular targets, specifically two-steppers, as we chase wins and strikeouts, hoping the Ratio Monster doesn’t eat our leads in ERA and WHIP. JR Ritchie and Daniel Lynch IV were the most added starters who we expect two starts from this week. Ritchie’s MLB debut back in April came with great promise, but walks haunted him greatly, which led to trips back to Triple-A to refine his craft and some bulk inning relief work when he returned to Atlanta in July. Ritchie was recently promoted again, and ran into a juggernaut Cubs offense last week, allowing six runs on seven hits in 4.2 innings. The walk rate (13.7%) isn’t pretty, and he has a good opportunity to end his season on a high note with two reasonable matchups — against the Reds at home and the Marlins on the road. Lynch had served the Royals well as their top southpaw out of the bullpen for most of the season. He moved to the rotation in August and slowly worked his pitch counts upward. Lynch has made it to five innings in each of his last three starts. His latest one (at HOU on September 16) went well — 5 IP – 2 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 3 K. More of that please as he faces the White Sox and Guardians at Kauffman Stadium in the final week. If I could only choose one for the week, it would be Ritchie.
Red Sox pitchers Brayan Bello and Garrett Whitlock were popular buys as the likelihood of roto stars shining bright on them this week is high. Bello is coming off a tremendous outing against the AL-leading Rays on Saturday where he posted an 11:0 K:BB with just one run allowed in eight innings. Those 11 punchies tied his career high. Bello had been the worst starter in the game (6.49 ERA, 1.67 WHIP) through June 4, when he was optioned to Triple-A. Since the All-Star break, mostly out of relief and with two starts, the 27-year-old has been shining. Over those 51.1 innings, he is rocking exemplary ratios (2.28 ERA, 1.01 WHIP) and a 17% K-BB% (22.3% K, 5.3% BB). Bello should make a start against the Cubs next Saturday. The Cubs should be settled into a playoff spot by then, so perhaps they give Pete Crow-Armstrong and some of the other regulars that day off. Boston’s closer Aroldis Chapman has been day-to-day with a lat issue, so perhaps the Red sox have him take it easy and provide Whitlock with some save opportunities. Whitlock has a 7-2 record with a 17.5 ERA, 0.88 WHIP and four saves.
Streaming Diamondbacks is a good idea this week, specifically for their three-game set at Coors Field against the Rockies in the early part of the week. Pavin Smith was a coveted target, coming off a four-day stretch where three of his hits were home runs. Don’t expect Smith to start against lefty Kyle Freeland, but he should be in the lineup for the other two contests against righties. Nolan Arenado was available in one of the 60 Main Event leagues and was acquired for just one dollar.
Better late than never for two punchless Padres who have been quite productive and certainly enjoyed their visit to Coors Field in the first half of last week. Dustin Harris ($10 AWB) and Samad Taylor ($5) have been red hot and playing often over the last 10 days. Though he doesn’t have a home run yet, Harris has been quite productive and helpful to early-bird managers: eight runs, 12 runs batted in and three steals, batting .384 with a 166 wRC+ in 40 plate appearances since September 11. He’s also been batting second against right-handed starters. Taylor has at least one hit in nine of his last 10, including a 3-for-3 effort on Sunday, and has driven in seven in his last seven games.

As always, more reliable starting pitcher depth was available in the 12-team OC pool. Cristian Javier, Anthony Kay, Robert Gasser, Lynch, Yusei Kikuchi, and Max Scherzer were the most added pitchers this week. Javier should pitch twice this week and will hope to put his best foot forward (in this case, his right arm) as the Astros fight for the AL West and a playoff spot. Sutter Health Park is not a fun place to pitch, but the A’s lineup is a watered-down version without Brent Rooker, Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, and Jacob Wilson윌슨. Javier’s first start is in Seattle may not be a picnic with gluten-free granola and Pearl Jam on the Discman.
Milwaukee’s Robert Gasser only draws one start (home vs. STL), but is considered a reliable ratios guy who can score a much-needed win for fantasy managers, as the Brewers will certainly be favorites in that matchup. Gasser earned his fifth win on Saturday, throwing seven scoreless innings against the Orioles. White Sox lefty Anthony Kay has good matchups (at KC on Tuesday and vs. COL on Sunday), though that second start could be pulled away from him. The main problems here is that Kay hasn’t made it to the fifth inning in any of his last five starts. I feel much more comfortable with a single start against the Orioles from Max Scherzer than I do a double (at SEA, at ATH) from wily Yusei Kikuchi. Kikuchi has walked 12 batters in his last three starts.

It’s possible that attraction towards Ryan Johnson this weekend relates to dynasty and keeper formats, and not his start in Seattle this week. Johnson has limited run damage over his last nine starts, since August 6, posting a 2.39 ERA, but with an xFIP (5.01) nearly double the mark. Johnson is more of a 4.25-4.50 ERA guy than a sub-3.00 ERA one, as his 90.9% LOB and .229 BABIP portends.
Perhaps a similar mindset applies to folks who scooped up Jack Perkins, who pitched two quality starts on the road against the Rays (6.2 IP – 4 H – 0 ER – 1 BB – 8 K) and the Guardians (6 IP – 5 H – 1 ER – 0 BB – 4 K), flashing some of his upside and future potential. Perkins has had a difficult season (5.90 ERA, but a 4.16 xFIP, 1.45 WHIP) and will be a tough streamer at home in Sacramento next season, but the strikeouts (25.2%) should always be there.
Andrew Alvarez should have a rotation spot with the Nationals next season. He has been outstanding since the All-Star break, posting a 2.44 ERA (3.30 FIP, 4.02 xFIP) with a 1.10 WHIP and a 22.7% strikeout rate, though he wasn’t able to secure a win in any of those 10 starts. Alvarez won’t be a particularly coveted target in drafts next season, but should have a NFBC ADP somewhere in the 250-325 overall range. He may be a consideration in NL-only keeper leagues with deep benches and five-plus keepers.
Bold Predictions for Week 27
Gavin Williams and Jacob Misiorowski finish the season tied for the MLB lead in strikeouts with 255. Williams punches out 11 and Misiorowski, eight.
JR Ritchie steps up for his two starts and has a Jack Perkins Week 26 type week, helping managers win league titles.
Cade Cavalli twirls a gem in Detroit this week and pulls his 3.02 ERA under 3.00 to end the season. Cavalli will have a top-60 ADP in 2027.
Jo Adell takes advantage of four left-handed starters this week and earns seven RBIs to reach 100, after falling two RBIs short last season.
One of Cristian Javier or Yusei Kikuchi will remind why streaming pitchers in Sutter Health Park, even if part of a two-step, is a mistake.
Miguel Vargas and Colson Montgomery hit three home runs each this week and the White Sox score the most runs in Week 27.
The Houston Astros win the NL West and knock the Texas Rangers out of playoff contention.
I hope you enjoyed my column this season and that you found it helpful, or at least entertaining and informative. Stay tuned for more from me next week as we hit the offseason streets. Best of luck this final week!

item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE – Somewhat fittingly for a team forced to make TBA a regular part of its starting rotation, Toronto Blue Jays ace Dylan Cease is finishing a Cy-Young calibre season in limbo after an MRI revealed inflammation but no structural damage to his right shoulder.
The 30-year-old, who’s struck out 239 in 169 innings while carrying a 2.40 ERA over 29 starts, said upon rejoining the team Monday that he and the club “are still drafting a plan” for his next steps, although he hasn’t been ruled out from starting again this year.
For him to pitch this weekend against the Cincinnati Reds, manager John Schneider said, Cease will need to be “feeling better with this time down and feeling like himself, and obviously the game meaning a lot” for the Blue Jays, who are nearing elimination in the wild-card race. If not, the first season of his $210-million, seven-year deal will have ended with a messy outing Friday in Texas where his career-low average fastball velocity of 93.6 m.p.h. was concerning enough for him to be sent out for imaging the day after.
“It’s good news, I'm not having surgery, there's nothing that's going to keep me out next year or anything like that,” said Cease. “It's just some inflammation of various kinds.”
Regardless, the disappointing way his season is ending is yet another blow for a Blue Jays rotation that lost Bowden Francis and Shane Bieber before spring training began, Trey Yesavage and Jose Berrios during camp, Cody Ponce 2.1 innings into his first start and Max Scherzer in late April, triggering an ongoing roster churn that had them opening the final week of the season with just two healthy starters.
Even after Yesavage’s activation from his second injured-list stint Monday to start against the Baltimore Orioles, the Blue Jays still had seven starters on the sidelines. A revolving door of arms made “trying to stay mentally positive about it” a challenge, said Schneider, while regular bullpen games meant extra strain on reliever workload not only on the day of, but the days before and the day after, too. There was so much up-and-down that three pitchers, Chad Dallas, also recalled Monday, Chase Lee and Lazaro Estrada, each were optioned the maximum five times allowed without needing to clear waivers.
All of that’s made sustained winning — a 15-14 May and a 17-11 August are their only winning months so far — especially difficult.
“I always say in order to win a few series in a row or to reel off seven or eight in a row, you've got to have a couple turns through the rotation that are pretty good,” said Schneider. “That's been hard to do this year.”
Throughout the season, Cease, along with Kevin Gausman until he was traded, held a threadbare staff together with elite innings every five days, helping to keep a struggling team afloat. But his velocity has been declining for a couple months and he first remembers his shoulder feeling “achy” before his July 25 one-hit, 120-pitch shutout at Boston.
Cease’s fastball averaged 95.8 m.p.h. that afternoon, his first time this season under 96, and hovered in that range through Sept. 2 before dropping to 94.9, 94.8, 93.6 in the three starts that followed.
“I've never really experienced this, it's always been pretty easy for me to throw hard effortlessly. I never really experienced max-effort throwing and it not coming out and all that,” said Cease. “But at the same time it still felt good to compete. And I feel like I've grown a lot as a pitcher in terms of using my pitch mix and executing and locating the fastball and stuff like that. It wasn't anything that was like end of the world. It was just kind of something that had to be dealt with and a part of trying to win is going out and taking the ball, no matter what.”
Trying to describe the feeling in his shoulder, Cease said, “I don't know if I would fully use the word painful, definitely a bit heavy and achy, just not normal,” and doesn’t believe it resulted from a single moment, but rather the wear and tear “of being a thrower.”
“I will say I think I learned a lot from this year in terms of going forward, how I maybe want to manage things a little better,” he said. “I've learned my body better from a season like this.”
Among the lessons he’s identified is the amount of throwing in-between bullpens he does and finding more opportunities to sneak in additional rest.
Bigger picture, the Blue Jays aim to search for some learnings as to why they’ve had so many pitching injuries this season. Other than playing in the World Series last year, there are no real through lines but they’ve already started looking.
“I think you look at each individual guy and what their workload was this year and what you can try to stay ahead of,” said Schneider. “I feel like we've done a fairly good job with that, with our relievers going back to spring training, trying to ease them in a little bit. And we'll have to look at that again with the number of appearances with some of these guys. We've already started to look at it and start thinking about throwing load in the off-season when it starts, how much rest is going to be needed before you do start and making sure that everyone comes in where they should be next year.”

BALTIMORE – Dylan Cease will not require surgery on his balky right shoulder, leaving the Toronto starting pitcher free to build back up over the off-season and follow up his Cy Young-caliber campaign with another good season in 2027.
The bad news is that Cease likely won't have a reason to return in 2026.
Cease said Monday, Sept. 21 that an MRI and other examinations determined inflammation in his shoulder, a relief to pitcher and club after he left his last start in the third inning with shoulder discomfort amid diminished velocity.
Cease, in the first season of a seven-year, $210 million contract, said his shoulder first felt funny as he warmed up for a July 25 start against Boston. He threw a one-hit shutout, striking out 12 that night, part of a 10-start run in which he posted a 1.89 ERA, struck out 89 in 62 innings and posted a 5-0 record.
But all the while, his velocity was diminishing. During his Friday start at Texas, the discomfort proved untenable. He walked six in 2 2/3 innings and gave up four runs, one earned, in an 11-6 loss at Texas.
"The velocity being down has been a little concerning but at the same time, I was getting outs," says Cease. "It wasn't anything too scary. Nothing about it feels like I need surgery. I was never really panicked or worried. Just more of an inconvenience that I couldn't maximize my best self.
"The last couple starts, velo kept going down and down and then command – that last one, it almost felt like I was hurting the team."
The Blue Jays lost both Cease's start and the next night at Texas, two defeats that were likely the fatal blows to their wild card hopes. Manager John Schneider said Monday that the club will assess both Cease's health and the relevance of their final three games against Cincinnati at Rogers Centre to determine if he'll pitch.
"Him feeling better, with this time down, and feeling like himself and obviously the game meaning a lot," says Schneider of the necessary conditions for a Cease return. "If those two things line up, hopefully he'll be good to go."
Toronto enters a three-game series at Baltimore with a 77-79 record, three games behind the Chicago White Sox for the final wild card, though the White Sox hold the tiebreaker so the deficit is effectively four games.
The Blue Jays do hold the tiebreaker over the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians, who lead them by 3 1/2 games, but their elimination number is three entering Monday.
Cease, 30, is enjoying the first All-Star season of his career. His 239 strikeouts in 169 innings have boosted him to atop the AL leaderboard in strikeouts per nine innings, at 12.7. His 2.40 ERA ranks second to Cy Young Award favorite Cam Schlittler and he leads the AL in fielding independent pitching (2.55).
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Dylan Cease gets good news on shoulder, but 2026 season probably over

item.content:encoded:
The Tampa Bay Rays, the New York Yankees, and the Boston Red Sox have all punched their ticket to the postseason. With the final week of the 2026 MLB regular season already upon us, several other American League squads are playing for a place in October, too.
Even the Rays and Yankees technically have to decide who wins the AL East, with the former enjoying a hefty advantage heading into the final week, needing just one win over the Bombers to secure it. After that, there are two wide-open divisions and an exciting competition for the last Wild Card spot.
Here’s where every team stands in the race:
Tampa Bay Rays
Remaining games: 4 @ Yankees, 3 @ Phillies
Current record: 95-60
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 1st in AL East (6 games ahead of NYY)
Final week outlook: The Rays have been, far and away, the top team in the American League by win-loss record, and unless something really crazy happens, they will enter the postseason with a first-round bye and wait for the winner of the battle between the top two Wild Cards—the Yankees and Red Sox—in the Division Series. They’ll still try to play competitive games after clinching, as they certainly wouldn’t say no to having home-field advantage over NL teams in a potential World Series matchup* as they seek their first championship in franchise history, but the pressure this week is much lighter.
*We’re keeping the focus on the AL in this post, but for those curious, Tampa Bay’s 95-60 record currently trails the Dodgers’ 96-60 and the Brewers’ 98-58. Atlanta trails at 92-64. The Dodgers have the Padres and Giants to end 2026 while the Brewers have the Phillies and Cardinals, and the Braves have the Reds and Marlins.
New York Yankees
Remaining games: 4 vs. Rays, 3 vs. Orioles
Current record: 89-66
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 2nd in AL East (6 games behind TB); 1st in Wild Card race (5.5 games ahead of 2nd Wild Card spot, held by BOS)
Final week outlook: Unless they sweep the Rays and Orioles, the Yankees virtually have no chance of winning the AL East crown. Instead, they will likely enter the postseason as the top Wild Card team, as they have a healthy cushion over the Red Sox, their likely foe in the Wild Card round. The odds of that series being at Fenway rather than Yankee Stadium are extremely low, especially since New York has the tiebreaker over Boston.
Boston Red Sox
Remaining games: 3 vs. Guardians, 3 vs. Cubs
Current record: 84-72
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 3rd in AL East, 2nd in Wild Card race (5.5 games behind NYY for top WC spot, 4 games ahead of CHW, owners of the 3rd WC spot)
Final week outlook: The Red Sox are highly unlikely to move from the second AL Wild Card spot, since they have a four-game cushion over the White Sox, owners of the third slot, and are 5.5 games behind the Yanks for the top one. They’ve been all but locked into this spot for awhile now and just clinched their playoff berth yesterday with Houston’s loss to Atlanta.
Cleveland Guardians
Remaining games: 3 @ Red Sox, 3 @ Royals
Current record: 81-75
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 1st in AL Central (1 game ahead of CHW)
Final week outlook: Eyeing their third consecutive division title and seventh since 2016, the Guardians are currently one game up in the race for the AL Central, but need to avoid a tie with the White Sox at the top because Chicago owns the tiebreaker. Cleveland is peaking at the right time, though, and José Ramírez is finally starting to show some signs of a breakthrough at the plate. If that’s the case, they will be dangerous with a strong young core and two aces at the top: AL strikeout leader Gavin Williams and Rookie of the Year contender Parker Messick. Second baseman Travis Bazzana isn’t too shabby of a rookie, either.
Chicago White Sox
Remaining games: 3 @ Royals, 3 vs. Rockies
Current record: 80-76
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 2nd in AL Central (1 game behind CLE), 3rd in Wild Card race (3 games ahead of HOU and TOR, 5 ahead of BAL)
Final week outlook: Chicago’s lack of quality starting pitching seems to have caught up to them in September, but they are still a dangerous team that is trending towards its first postseason appearance since 2021. They have a chance to win the AL Central: all they need to do is finish in at least a tie with the Guardians, and though both the Pale Hose and Guards will face the Royals this week, the Southsiders have an easier other foe in the Rockies. Remember, winning the division would likely even give Chicago the second seed in the AL and a first-round bye to face the victor of the AL West/last Wild Card matchup.
It’s already been an improbably great season for the White Sox, as merely getting a winning season would’ve been a huge success for a team that lost a modern record 121 games in 2024 and 102 last year. But missing out at this point would still be quite the disappointment.
Texas Rangers
Remaining games: 3 vs. Mets, 3 @ Twins
Current record: 78-78
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 1st in AL West (1 game ahead of HOU)
Final week outlook: If the Rangers finish with more wins than the Astros, they will capture the AL West despite their thoroughly mediocre record (the Mariners’ deeply disappointing 2026 really made the division a mess). It’s a key week in Texas, as the range of outcomes is wide: they could win the division and finish as high as the second seed if they can best the AL Central champ’s line; they could be the final Wild Card squad, or they could miss the playoffs entirely for the third year in a row since winning it all in 2023 behind two-time World Series MVP Corey Seager.
It’s important to note that the Rangers need to beat the Astros by at least one game to take the AL West crown because Houston owns the tiebreaker. The Rangers own tiebreakers against the Orioles, Guardians, and Blue Jays, and lost against the White Sox and, as explained, the Astros. The AL West winner is a near-lock to face the worst Wild Card team in the first round, though they will host the best-of-three.
Toronto Blue Jays
Remaining games: 3 @ Orioles, 3 vs. Reds
Current record: 77-79
Current position in division/Wild Card race: tied with HOU for 4th in Wild Card standings, 3 games behind the 3rd spot (CHW)
Final week outlook: Last year’s AL champs can’t win their division: their only path to the playoffs is the third and final Wild Card spot. With that in mind, however, they would need to finish ahead of both the White Sox and the Rangers because both of them own the tiebreaker against Toronto. It sure doesn’t help that ace Dylan Cease was scratched from his next start and is undergoing an MRI.
The Jays tied the season series against Houston, which, in the event of a tie at the third WC spot between them, would take us to intra-divisional record to decide. There, Toronto is 25-24 against AL East opponents, and the Astros are 22-24 vs. AL West foes, presently giving the Jays the edge, though that could change this week since they both face intra-divisional rivals.
For what it’s worth, Toronto won the tiebreakers against the Guardians and the Orioles.
Houston Astros
Remaining games: 2 @ Mariners, 4 @ A’s
Current record: 77-79
Current position in division/Wild Card race: tied with TOR for 4th in Wild Card standings, 3 games behind the 3rd spot (CHW)
Final week outlook: Much like the White Sox in the AL Central, the Astros are one game behind in their division and own the tiebreaker against the Rangers, so all they need to do is catch them by the end of the week. They have lost three straight, though, with a -59 run differential, so despite the best efforts of MVP frontrunner Yordan Alvarez, they aren’t particularly good. We have seen plenty of mediocre squads make it in the past, so they definitely have a chance — especially since they get to play the mostly-hapless M’s and A’s this week.
Houston can still qualify via the last Wild Card, but the division presents a smoother path. Since we’re running through them, they own tiebreakers vs. the White Sox, Guardians, and Rangers, losing vs. the Orioles and tying vs. Toronto.
Baltimore Orioles
Remaining games: 3 vs. Blue Jays, 3 @ Yankees
Current record: 75-81
Current position in division/Wild Card race: 6th in Wild Card standings, 5 games behind the 3rd spot (CHW)
Final week outlook: At this point, the Orioles need a miracle to get in. They needed to sweep the Brewers this past weekend to put themselves in a position to compete. Instead, they got swept themselves. Baltimore won tiebreakers against the White Sox and the Astros, and lost against the Rangers, Guardians, and Blue Jays. But again, they have essentially no shot whatsoever. That final weekend series in the Bronx could’ve been interesting; alas.

item.content:encoded:
The playoffs technically don't start for another week or so, but good luck telling that to teams for which every game already feels like October. With the standings in both the NL and AL as jumbled as they've been in recent memory, the stakes are already as high as can be — and whoever gets hot now could well ride that wave all the way to a World Series.
"Hot" could definitely describe both the San Diego Padres and Cleveland Guardians of late. The former has decided to just never lose again, not only grabbing hold of a Wild Card spot but now pushing for home-field in the first round if things break right. The latter, meanwhile, has once again snatched the AL Central while no one was looking. And they're not the only ones making serious moves in our latest MLB power rankings.
But who are we buying as serious title contenders, and who still has work to do? Read on to find out.
30. Colorado Rockies
The Rockies have admittedly let go of the rope of late, well on their way to yet another 100-loss season. There are at least some promising young hitters in this organization, which represents something to build upon moving forward. Of course, the pitching staff remains a mess, and no one's been able to crack that nut yet in Colorado.
–Chris Landers, FanSided.com editor
29. Los Angeles Angels
In Reid Detmers, Walbert Urena and Ryan Johnson, the Angels have at least some sort of foundation upon which to build for the future. Well, OK, maybe not Detmers, who will almost certainly be dealt this offseason. But still, L.A.’s pitching staff has been a real bright spot of late. The offense … well, that’s another question. Things are going to get worse before they get better under John Mozeliak. At least Arte Moreno is no longer around to meddle in it.
–CL
28. Athletics
The A’s are playing out the string of a lost season, although the contributions they’ve gotten from young bats like Henry Bolte, Max Muncy (not that one), Lawrence Butler and Zack Gelof down the stretch have been notable. None of that will matter, though, until the team fixes its pitching staff. We know we sound like a broken record, but it really is that simple, and no potential answers have emerged in the second half.
–CL
27. San Francisco Giants
Rafael Devers' injury, which figures to cost him at least some of next season as well as the end of this one, is a fitting if unfortunate end to what's been a miserable season by the Bay. Devers had been one of the few bright spots on this Giants team down the stretch alongside Bryce Eldridge; now, it's unclear how San Francisco will rebuilt its offense for 2027 in addition to finding reinforcements for a pitching staff that simply hasn't been good enough.
–CL
26. Kansas City Royals
The Kansas City Royals have been eliminated for quite some time now. If there is one clear goal for Kansas City this winter, it's to build a roster around Bobby Witt Jr. that is capable of making a postseason run. That is every team's goal, but the Royals are so far away from contention despite featuring such a prolific player, Witt Jr.'s career is closer to becoming Mike Trout's than Derek Jeter's.
-Mark Powell, FanSided.com MLB director
25. Minnesota Twins
At one point not all that long ago, the Twins had a realistic chance to make the playoffs as the third AL Wild Card spot. Then, the bottom fell out. Byron Buxton underwent successful hip surgery just last week that will keep him out until spring training, whenever that may be. The Twins once again experienced the roster flaw of building around an injured star.
-MP
24. New York Mets
This week couldn’t have been more awkward for the New York Mets when Pete Alonso hit his 300th home run in his return to Citi Field, much to the delight of many Mets fans in attendance, but once Alonso left town, the Mets began to play better, winning two games in a row against the Phillies. Those wins, headlined by more quality play from youngsters like Carson Benge, Zac Thornton and Christian Scott, show why Mets fans should be somewhat enthusiastic for what’s to come.
–Zach Rotman, FanSided.com staff writer
23. Cincinnati Reds
In the American League, the Reds likely wouldn't be the worst team in their division. But the NL Central has been a gauntlet all year long, and the Reds couldn't keep up. Despite breakthrough seasons from Elly De La Cruz and Sal Stewart, Cincinnati still has a long way to go on the starting pitching front. Can they rely on Hunter Greene and Chase Burns moving forward?
-MP
22. Seattle Mariners
Going 3-3 against the Angels and Rockies this week just about sums up this season in Seattle. The good news is that youngsters like Michael Arroyo and Lazaro Montes have helped to key an offensive turnaround. The bad news is that the starting rotation hasn’t held up its end of the bargain of late, and there are still tons of long-term questions about this lineup — especially with Randy Arozarena set to hit free agency. Jerry DiPoto will need to find some answers this offseason after a year in which just about everything went wrong.
–CL
21. Washington Nationals
The Washington Nationals deserved a better fate in 2026. Even with their offense falling off a bit of late, they’re still third in the majors in runs scored. The dynamic duo of CJ Abrams and James Wood is as good as any in the National League. Recently extended Cade Cavalli is a budding ace. Andrew Alvarez has thrown the ball incredibly well and looks like a future rotation stalwart. If it weren’t for a historically bad bullpen, we’d be talking about this team in Wild Card contention.
–ZR
20. Detroit Tigers
The Tigers have the best run differential in the AL Central and a pythagorean record of an AL playoff team. None of it matters. Scott Harris and the Tigers front office gave up on their team's postseason hopes at the trade deadline. Then, they proceeded to get fans' hopes up with a late August run, only to play like the team Harris assumed they'd become when it mattered most. The Tigers have some work to do, though the emergence of young stars in the lineup like Hao-Yu Lee and Kevin McGonigle, paired with Riley Greene's consistent play, give them some building blocks.
-MP
19. St. Louis Cardinals
The Cardinals are ahead of schedule, but not a postseason team. Make no mistake about it, St. Louis came crashing back down to earth in September, and has been eliminated from playoff contention. There are questions about the long-term future of Masyn Winn, especially with JJ Wetherholt as the de-facto shortstop of the future. But these are all good problems to have. Now, if only Bloom could find an ace burried in that farm system of his.
-MP
18. Baltimore Orioles
A series against league-best Milwaukee came at the worst possible time for the O’s, which now find themselves needing to hit an inside straight to snatch the final Wild Card spot. Pete Alonso’s heroics at Citi Field aside, Baltimore’s bats simply have not been good enough. Heck, no part of this team has; they’re hovering around .500 for a reason, after all, and there’s no reason to think they have the consistency required to get hot over the final week and overtake the White Sox, Blue Jays and Astros.
–CL
17. Miami Marlins
The Miami Marlins tried to do what they could to stick around in the NL postseason hunt, even using Sandy Alcantara on one day of rest in a save opportunity, but they were eliminated following Friday’s loss in San Diego. As disappointing as that is, the Marlins could finish above .500 for just the third time since 2009. That’s a sign that things are heading in the right direction for Miami.
–ZR
16. Toronto Blue Jays
The Jays have lost three of four series now, and news that Dylan Cease will have his next start bumped due to shoulder fatigue makes it even less likely that Toronto can sneak its way into the playoffs. With Trey Yesavage and Shane Bieber already on the IL, the rotation has begun leaking oil, and that’s not something this power-starved lineup is equipped to handle. The Jays still have a path to the final Wild Card spot, but it’s becoming an increasingly tenuous one, and it’s hard to see them making much noise even if they did get in.
–CL
15. Houston Astros
Getting swept at home by the Braves this weekend might well wind up costing the Astros a playoff spot. The closing schedule isn’t too tough, with trips to Seattle and Sacramento on tap. Still, if Houston doesn’t figure out where its high-powered offense went before it’s too late — and if Joe Espada can’t stop his bullpen from blowing late leads — Yordan Alvarez’s MVP season may well be for nought. As it stands, this looks like a team with fatal flaws that will spoil what could have been a deep run in a wide-open AL.
–CL
14. Chicago White Sox
Reality hit the White Sox real quick. Chicago has lingered around .500 for longer than they'd care to admit, and it was only a matter of time before the rest of the Central caught up to them. Munetaka Murakami has been dreadful since the trade deadline, and thus any contract extension talks have been put on hold. If the White Sox can hold on to a playoff spot, they'll be one of the best stories in October. If not, this season could all be for naught.
-MP
13. Texas Rangers
All of a sudden, the Rangers find themselves back in control of the AL West and home-field advantage in the first round of the playoffs. Of course, that says more about the West than it does about Texas; this is still a .500 team, one without a ton of depth on either side of the ball. The interesting thing, though, is that this lineup has finally started to show signs of life of late. Take care of business against the Twins and Mets this week, and no one’s going to want to face a team with Jacob deGrom and Nathan Eovaldi in the rotation plus an offense featuring Corey Seager, Wyatt Langford and Josh Jung.
-CL
12. Pittsburgh Pirates
The narrative Pirates fans are spinning these days is the same web every National League non-playoff team will get caught in this week; if only we played in the American League! Yes, the disparity between leagues is easy to blame for the Pirates shortcomings, but the front office also fell short in acquiring bullpen arms last winter, which could've kept Pittsburgh from blowing an extraordinary number of leads in the season's first half. That'll haunt these Pirates forever.
-MP
11. Arizona Diamondbacks
It's not Arizona's fault that their primary competition for a Wild Card spot, San Diego, has become one of the hottest teams in baseball over the last few weeks. Either way, though, Arizona has simply run out of bullets, especially in a rotation that hasn't gotten the boost from Corbin Burnes' return that they were hoping for. Eduardo Rodriguez has turned back into a pumpkin, and there's just not enough depth to keep pace with what's become a beast of an NL playoff chase.
–CL
10. Cleveland Guardians
Here we go again with the Guardians. Cleveland is a legitimate threat in a weak American League. Much like last season, the Guards are taking advantage of a fellow contender floundering down the stretch. This is when Cleveland plays its best baseball, so it should be no surprise they've won five straight games heading into Monday's potential postseason preview against the Red Sox.
-MP
9. Boston Red Sox
Dropping consecutive series to the Rangers and Rays won’t do much to Boston’s postseason outlook — they’ve been more or less locked into a Wild Card series in the Bronx for a while now — but it still doesn’t inspire confidence in this team’s ability to make a run come October. This offense is once again mired in a power outage, and while getting Willson Contreras and others back from the IL figures to help, who knows when that might actually be. And there’s still just a real dearth of power here that even this pitching staff might not be able to make up for.
–CL
8. Philadelphia Phillies
I don’t know what to think of the Philadelphia Phillies. On one hand, a rotation led by Zack Wheeler, Cristopher Sanchez, a healthy Jesus Luzardo, a rejuvenated Aaron Nola and a much-improved Andrew Painter should will them to wins. On the other hand, Luzardo is not healthy, the lineup is top-heavy and the bullpen, outside of Jhoan Duran, is an utter disaster. The Phillies are almost certainly going to make the playoffs, but their losses in New York this week ruined any last hope they had at a division title. And with how they’re playing right now, I don’t know if I’d pick them to get beyond the Wild Card Round.
–ZR
7. Chicago Cubs
The Cubs playoff parade was put on hold Sunday as Alex Bregman was struck in the face by a foul ball. Bregman was taken to the local hospital, and it's unclear how much time he will miss as of this writing. Chicago's postseason hopes may hang in the balance, as their one clear advantage over every other NL team is their lineup. The Cubs have scored the most runs in baseball this year.
-MP
6. San Diego Padres
Yes, the schedule has helped, particularly series against Miami, Colorado, Washington, San Francisco and Cincinnati. But no matter who they've played, the Padres look like a different team from the one we saw for much of the year, with their big bats finally mashing and their rotation coming into focus with Nick Pivetta now back in the fold. San Diego is now dead even with Chicago and Philly in the Wild Card race, and no one will want to face this lineup and this bullpen in a short series.
–CL
5. New York Yankees
Just when it seemed like New York was getting ready to make a move, with Aaron Judge finally back in the lineup after months on the shelf, the reigning AL MVP landed right back on the IL — this time with a calf strain that could well jeopardize his entire postseason. It’s been that sort of year for the Yankees, which have the pitching to keep believing in them as contenders but just haven’t been able to put it all together enough to take command of their own playoff destiny. And with a Judge-less offense and a penchant for mistake-filled baseball, winning three series in a row feels like a tough ask even in this AL.
–CL
4. Atlanta Braves
The Atlanta Braves punched their ticket to the playoffs this week, and thanks to the Phillies’ struggles, they’re on the cusp of winning the NL East — ensuring a top-three seed in the National League. Tyler Mahle pitched another gem, and Ronald Acuña Jr. is hitting his stride at the perfect time. There’re still some concerns with the team, like the No. 3 spot in their rotation and struggling stars like Austin Riley and Ozzie Albies, but getting to the playoffs is a big deal, and the Braves can take pride in checking that box.
–ZR
3. Tampa Bay Rays
The Rays may well have sewn up the AL East this week, taking two of three from the Red Sox over the weekend to stretch their lead over the Yankees ahead of an all-important four-game set in the Bronx beginning on Tuesday. Even if New York were to sweep all four, though, Tampa would still have the inside track to the division and the No. 1 overall seed. This pitching staff continues to thrive beyond all expectation even with some recent injuries, and the hitting has done just enough. Whether that recipe will withstand the postseason is the only question now.
–CL
2. Los Angeles Dodgers
Don't look now, but L.A.'s lineup has begun to stir, with Kyle Tucker looking like the player the Dodgers thought they were paying for this offseason. They also got Edwin Diaz back this week, and he's suddenly looking like the star closer of old — potentially answering this team's biggest question entering October. We know the rotation will be there; if they have Tucker at the height of his powers and a one-two punch in Diaz and Tanner Scott at the end of games, the three-peat march might be back on.
–CL
1. Milwaukee Brewers
The Brewers set a franchise record with 98 wins on Sunday. They still have a full week to go to add to that mark, and appear likely to reach the 100-win plateau. That's a great accomplishment, but it won't mean squat if Milwaukee falls to the Los Angeles Dodgers — or any other NL team for that matter — on their way to that elusive NL pennant. The Brewers are the favorites, but the Dodgers are lingering right behind them.
-MP

item.content:encoded:
Bobby Witt Jr. is having a down year. He’s running his worst batting line in three seasons. He’s in danger of missing the 20-homer threshold for the first time in his career. A lower back injury in July will also limit him to a career low in games played. Put it together, and Witt is on pace to put up his the lowest WAR total since his 5.9-win 2023 campaign. Oh, and he also grabbed hold of the American League lead in WAR back in July and still hasn’t relinquished it. A down year by Bobby Witt Jr.’s standards is still good enough to make him a deserving MVP.
I don’t know if Witt is going to win his first MVP this year. Ours is the only flavor of WAR in which he leads the AL, and he leads by just a quarter of a win. He ranks third by Baseball Reference’s rWAR and is eighth by Baseball Prospectus’ WARP. Yordan Alvarez leads all of baseball in WARP because he’s hitting like, well, Yordan Alvarez and staying healthy like, well, someone other than Yordan Alvarez. Cam Schlittler leads the AL in Baseball Reference WAR, and he’s been so dominant that he deserves consideration for the Cy Young-MVP combo — if only he’d pitched just 23 fewer innings last year, he could’ve gone for the trifecta with Rookie of the Year. Kevin McGonigle has played like an MVP from the moment he arrived in Detroit, and Junior Caminero has surpassed 40 home runs for the second season in a row as a 23-year-old. All of these guys have a case, and they aren’t the only ones who merit inclusion in the discussion:
